final.memo:
Our investment in Upstart began in the venture stage, providing us with a deep understanding of their AI-driven credit-underwriting technology [D01]. Unlike a transient public-market bet, this position reflects our comfort with the company’s ability to improve approval and loss outcomes via its partner-bank ecosystem [D01]. 

Following the IPO, the business has demonstrated promising operating momentum, with Q3 2020 revenues reaching $65.36 million, a 32.1% increase over the prior-year period [D03]. Operating margins have improved significantly, though we remain focused on the durability of this fee-based model through a full credit cycle [D03, D06]. 

The rapid rerating of the share price to $62.19, roughly three times the IPO price, has reduced the immediate margin of safety [D04]. While we are pleased with the market’s reception, we are not adding at these levels; we prefer to wait for additional public disclosures regarding loan-cohort performance and funding stability before sizing up [D03, D05]. We maintain a HOLD position to allow the management team to execute against their stated objectives while we monitor the risks of model sensitivity in untested economic conditions [D03, D05].
